## Classification Note

All 12 in-scope stories carry an explicit `Type:` field in their header, set by the owning
programmer/specialist at story creation. Per `/qa-plan` protocol these are accepted **as-is, not
re-classified**:

| Story | Priority | Declared Type |
|---|---|---|
| building-002 (Project entity + rollup) | Must | Logic |
| building-004 (Release + job-eligibility) | Must | Logic |
| building-030 (Construction job queue) | Must | **Integration** |
| villager-ai-010 (F2 job selection) | Must | Logic |
| villager-ai-011 (Job claim/release + attribution) | Must | **Integration** |
| villager-ai-012 (On-site work + full cycle — **THE CROWN**) | Must | **Integration** |
| building-005 (Worker attribution) | Should | **Integration** |
| building-032 (Undo/redo stack core) | Should | Logic |
| presentation-001 Sub-A (Ambient life, environmental) | Should | Visual/Feel |
| building-033 (Voxel World write seam) | Nice | **Integration** |
| building-003 (Grouping/merge + reverse index) | Nice | Logic |
| villager-ai-025 (30-villager perf stress) | Nice | **Integration** (self-declared Advisory/Performance — see Call-out 1) |

**6 of 6 Must stories are Logic or Integration — 100% BLOCKING on the critical path**, matching every
prior sprint's precedent. Should adds one more BLOCKING Integration (005) and one more BLOCKING Logic
(032), plus one ADVISORY Visual/Feel (presentation-001 Sub-A — the sprint's only primary V/F story,
same posture as a "no primary V/F story" sprint would have on the BLOCKING side, but this sprint does
have one). Nice adds two more BLOCKING-if-pulled stories (033 Integration, 003 Logic) and one
self-declared-Advisory Integration (025).

**Five call-outs flagged for producer/technical-director visibility, not resolved unilaterally here:**

1. **villager-ai-025 declares `Type: Integration` but its own header carves itself out of the BLOCKING
   gate.** Its Context section states outright: "AC39 is an Advisory/Performance criterion... not part
   of the Logic gate," and its Test Evidence section separates a `tests/performance/` file (not
   `tests/integration/`) plus a recorded envelope doc. This is a legitimate, story-declared exception —
   Performance-class Integration stories are advisory by their own GDD provenance (ADR-0008/0007's
   measured-envelope tradition, same posture as Sprint 6's spike reports) — but it means the "Integration
   = BLOCKING" rule has exactly one named exception this sprint. Flagging so nobody reads a red
   `stress_30_villager_test.gd` as a sprint-gating failure; it informs the Sprint 8 re-tune decision
   (criterion #4), it does not block villager-ai-025's own Done status at MVP scope, and it does not
   block anything else's Done.

2. **building-030's AC21/AC36b are explicitly PROVISIONAL** in its own Acceptance Criteria ("GIVEN a
   real villager... integration test once that GDD lands") — this sprint is exactly when that GDD lands.
   villager-ai-012's own AC40 ("closes Building AC21") is the story that resolves this PROVISIONAL tag.
   This plan therefore treats **AC21/AC36b as closed by villager-ai-012's crown test, not by
   building-030's own test file** — building-030's own `construction_job_queue_test.gd` continues to
   cover only its mocked halves (queue ordering, on-site predicate, occupied-defer, unreachable-ghost
   signal). Flagging so nobody expects a second, separate "real cycle" test inside building-030's own
   file — that evidence lives in `build_job_cycle_test.gd`.

3. **building-005's "full claim→build→report cycle is PROVISIONAL pending Villager AI" is ambiguous
   now that the real cycle exists in-sprint.** Story-005's own Test Evidence still says "mocked-claim
   unit-level test acceptable now," written before this sprint's dependency chain closed. Since
   villager-ai-012's crown test uses REAL Building System components and drives a real claim through
   villager-ai-011, it is a natural place to also assert `on_job_claimed` fired and `worker_ids` on the
   project now contains the claiming villager id — closing 005's PROVISIONAL alongside AC40, at
   negligible extra cost. **No story's Test Evidence section names this assertion explicitly** — this
   plan recommends adding it as an extra case in `build_job_cycle_test.gd` (see Automated Tests
   Required, villager-ai-012). If the team elects not to add it, building-005 remains PROVISIONAL and
   its mocked-claim test is still sufficient for building-005's own Done status (it is Should, not
   gating the crown) — but the milestone-relevant fact ("attribution proven against a real claim") would
   go unrecorded this sprint. Flagging for a decision, not mandating the extra assertion unilaterally.

4. **presentation-001 Sub-A's own Test Evidence text says CD sign-off is "mandatory, not advisory"** —
   read at face value this appears to conflict with `coding-standards.md`'s ADVISORY gate level for
   Visual/Feel stories. Resolving the apparent tension: **ADVISORY, in this plan's usage, describes the
   evidence's relationship to the SPRINT gate** (a missing or pending presentation-001 sign-off does not
   block villager-ai-012, building-030, or any other story's Done status, and does not block the smoke
   hand-off) — it is not a claim that CD sign-off is optional for presentation-001 ITSELF. The story's
   own "mandatory" language refers to that second, narrower sense: CD sign-off is the binding acceptance
   gate for presentation-001's own Done status specifically (per its CD-protected M01 tag), exactly as
   coding-standards.md's ADVISORY table entry already implies ("Screenshot + lead sign-off," required
   evidence, just not a cross-story blocker). No actual conflict — flagging only because the wording
   invites a misread.

5. **Sprint 7's own DoD names only villager-ai-012's own test file (`build_job_cycle_test.gd`) — it does
   not explicitly require extending Sprint 6's assembled-GameWorld E2E test
   (`gameworld_e2e_loop_test.gd`) to the worker-driven path.** This plan treats that extension as the
   sprint's **smoke item #1** anyway, per the delegated QA task and per Sprint 6's own precedent (its
   smoke item 2 explicitly requires re-running the E2E test "even if it passed at scene-004's own
   story-completion time," because later stories touching shared wiring can silently break it — this
   sprint's whole point is exactly that: villager-ai-010/011/012 + building-002/004/030 all touch the
   wiring scene-004 assembled). **Verified directly against the current file**
   (`neues-spiel/tests/integration/scene_world/gameworld_e2e_loop_test.gd`): line 262 calls
   `loop.claim_job(target, 1)` manually, and line 306 assigns `villager.job_queue = jobs` directly — both
   are exactly the "seams" sprint-07.md's own Notes name ("`ConstructionTickLoop.claim_job`, villager
   `job_queue` duck-type... let the crown *assemble* the two halves") as what this sprint's real
   release→queue→select→claim machinery must replace. Flagging so producer/technical-director confirm
   this is the intended interpretation — this plan is *adding* a requirement sprint-07.md's DoD prose
   does not spell out, not inventing a new story.

## Automated Tests Required

### building-002 — Project entity + blueprint-cell lifecycle rollup — Logic
**Test file path**: `neues-spiel/tests/unit/building_system/project_entity_lifecycle_test.gd`

**What to test**:
- AC60: a project whose every cell reaches Built/Removed rolls up to DONE and the entity is NOT
  deleted.
- AC61: a project whose last remaining cell is canceled (Draft) or demolished/excavated away (Built)
  has its entity removed — the sole deletion condition.
- Rollup correctness: mixed Built + Draft cells yield a non-DONE state; a Canceled cell is never
  reachable from Built.
- Draft-cell invisibility: `claim_job` returns none of a DRAFT project's cells.

**Edge cases to cover**:
- A project with exactly one Built cell and no pending batch is DONE, not deleted (the "single-cell
  DONE" boundary).
- Deleting a DONE project's last cell via demolition removes the entity (DONE is not a protected
  state against the deletion rule).

**Estimated test count**: ~5-6

---

### building-004 — Release ("Bau starten") + job-eligibility transition — Logic
**Test file path**: `neues-spiel/tests/unit/building_system/release_job_eligibility_test.gd`

**What to test**:
- AC57: `release_project` flips every Draft cell to BUILDING/job-eligible; none were claimable before
  the call.
- `claim_job` gating: given DRAFT, BUILDING, PAUSED, and an unreleased change-order batch
  side-by-side, only BUILDING cells are offered.
- Queue ordering by commit time (t1 < t2 < t3) — advisory for display/tie-break, not forced servicing.

**Edge cases to cover**:
- Releasing an empty project is a no-op (no error, no phantom jobs).
- A DRAFT project's cells are never claimable pre-release (negative case companion to AC57).

**Estimated test count**: ~5-6

### villager-ai-010 — F2 job selection (nearest-reachable, bounded candidates) — Logic
**Test file path**: `neues-spiel/tests/unit/villager_ai/job_selection_f2_test.gd`

**What to test** (HIGH engine-risk — consumes villager-ai-007's AStar3D true-path API, cross-reference
`docs/engine-reference/godot/` before trusting any candidate-check assumption):
- AC6: selection returns the true-path-nearest among the Chebyshev-nearest `job_candidate_count`
  candidates; ties break older-commit → lexicographic (y, x, z) — deterministic across two runs.
- AC7: if the first `job_candidate_count` all fail true-path, the next round is tried, deterministically,
  up to `max_selection_candidates` — assert pathfind-attempt count ≤ `max_selection_candidates`, not
  just "eventually returns."
- Fall-through: all candidates within the cap fail → the pass yields "none reachable" (delegated
  handling), not an error or an infinite retry loop within this call.
- "Available" = queue-non-empty only — reachability is never a pre-filter gate on the ranking itself
  (assert an unreachable-but-nearest candidate is still attempted, not silently skipped from ranking).

**Edge cases to cover**:
- Exactly `max_selection_candidates` candidates all fail → fall-through, no (`max_selection_candidates`
  + 1)-th attempt.
- A queue that is non-empty but every candidate is unreachable.

**Estimated test count**: ~6-7

### villager-ai-011 — Job claim/release pipeline with worker attribution — Integration
**Test file path**: `neues-spiel/tests/integration/villager_ai/job_claim_attribution_test.gd`

**What to test** (this story's own dependency set is 010 + 006 only — it does NOT depend on
building-030 in-sprint, so its own test necessarily exercises a mocked/duck-typed job queue; **the
race assertion this implies must be re-verified at smoke time against the REAL queue once building-030
lands — see Smoke Test Scope, Race/Ordering Assertions, item (a)**):
- AC8 / Edge Case 3 — **the deterministic-winner race assertion, named explicitly, not folded into a
  generic "claim works" line**: two villagers race the same job in one tick; assert the winner is
  exactly the earlier villager in stable processing order, and assert this is identical across
  repeated runs (determinism, not "usually the same villager"). The loser must proceed cleanly to its
  next F2 candidate in the SAME pass — assert it does not stall in Deciding or throw.
- AC9: pathing failure to a claimed job → reported to the Building System, claim released, next
  candidate tried.
- AC10/AC11: unreachable retry after `unreachable_retry_ticks`; all-unreachable in one pass → falls
  through to Wandering (never stuck in Deciding), retries resume on cadence.
- AC58: on successful claim, the claiming villager's id is recorded on the claim record and retrievable
  for `worker_ids` aggregation.
- Sticky claims: a periodic re-check with no preemption/revocation/pathing-failure does NOT re-select a
  held job (no argmin oscillation mid-travel).
- AC43: two villagers with simultaneous urgent-sleep targeting the same unowned bed → exactly one
  succeeds atomically via the SAME primitive as AC8's job contention; the loser falls back per Rule 12.

**Edge cases to cover**:
- The winner/loser assertion must hold under a THIRD villager racing the same job in the same tick (not
  just two) — stable order still picks exactly one winner.
- A released claim (AC9) is immediately re-offerable to any villager, including the one that just
  released it.

**Estimated test count**: ~8-9

### villager-ai-012 — On-site work & full claim→build→report cycle — THE CROWN — Integration
**Test file path**: `neues-spiel/tests/integration/villager_ai/build_job_cycle_test.gd` (uses REAL
Building System components — no mocked queue, no mocked project entity)

**What to test** (HIGH risk — the historical failure mode is wiring gaps at real-system assembly;
structure each stage as an independently-diagnosable assertion, same discipline as Sprint 6's crown):
- AC12: off-site (not target, not orthogonally adjacent incl. above/below) → zero progress accrual;
  on-site → progress accrues.
- AC13: arrival between two ticks → the first progress increment credits at the NEXT tick boundary,
  never partially — assert no fractional-tick credit exists as an intermediate state.
- **AC40 — the full cycle, closes Building AC21**: a real villager claims (via 011, against the REAL
  building-030 queue) → travels (via 009) → accrues ticks on-site → the cell transitions to Built via
  the Building System's real write → the job is removed from the real queue → the villager re-enters
  Deciding. Assert each stage independently: claim recorded, `current_cell` arrival, tick-boundary
  progress ticks, the Built-state write, the queue no longer offering that cell, and the villager's FSM
  state == Deciding post-completion.
- AC40b: a builder deferred by an occupied target (building-030's AC36) resumes progress on the next
  tick once the occupant vacates (F4), WITHOUT re-claiming the job — assert the claim record is
  unchanged across the defer/resume boundary (same claim, not claim→release→re-claim).
- AC33: a job revoked mid-work (player undo/removal) → the villager stops at the tick boundary (not
  mid-cell), plays no failure reaction, and re-enters Deciding without error.
- **Recommended addition (Call-out 3, not currently named in any story's Test Evidence)**: after the
  real claim in the AC40 flow, assert the project's `worker_ids` (building-005's aggregate) contains the
  claiming villager's id — closes building-005's PROVISIONAL tag alongside AC40 at negligible cost. Add
  only if building-005 has landed by the time this file is written; otherwise note its absence
  explicitly rather than silently skip it.
- **Race/ordering assertion (Call-out 5 / Smoke item 2(b) and 2(c) — defined by this plan, not named in
  any story's own Test Evidence)**:
  - Claim-released-on-abandon survives the real queue: drive AC33's revoke path, then assert the
    released job is genuinely re-offered by the REAL building-030 queue and claimable by a second
    villager — not merely that `release()` was called. This is the load-bearing regression check for
    villager-ai-009's AC19 (Sprint 6, proven against a mocked/duck-typed queue) now that a real queue
    exists.
  - Completion reporting exactly once: assert the Built-state write fires exactly once and the
    job-removed-from-queue event fires exactly once for one completed job, even when driven through a
    multi-tick burst (building-029's AC25/AC45 burst rule) — no double-credit, no duplicate completion
    signal.

**Edge cases to cover**:
- A half-failure is diagnosable in isolation: if the claim stage fails, the on-site/AC12/AC13 assertions
  should still be constructible and report independently (mirrors Sprint 6's scene-004 guardrail).
- This test genuinely depends on villager-ai-011 AND building-030 landing — if either slips, do not stub
  around the missing dependency to force a green AC40; an honestly-red crown is better than a
  falsely-green one (Sprint 6 precedent, scene-004's own Edge Case note).

**Estimated test count**: ~9-11 (5 named ACs + the worker_ids addition + the 2 race/ordering additions,
each with at least one boundary case)

### building-032 — Undo/redo stack core (Should) — Logic
**Test file path**: `neues-spiel/tests/unit/building_system/undo_redo_stack_core_test.gd`

**What to test**:
- AC28: an undone command redone with some cells now occupied → only still-valid cells re-created,
  invalid ones dropped with feedback; a zero-survivor redo is a no-op with feedback.
- AC30: at `undo_stack_depth` capacity, a new command silently discards the oldest.
- AC31: any prior undo + a new command commits → the redo branch clears.
- AC32 / AC32b: a transition that COMPLETES clears the stack; a transition that ABORTS leaves all
  commands undoable — no begin-signal side effect touches the stack.
- **Plan-only guardrail (control-manifest, extends the Sprint 6 grep-guard family to this story's new
  stack code)**: grep/assert the undo/redo code paths reference only Draft/Planned cell state and the
  ghost/blueprint write API — zero calls into the Building System's committed-block (Built-cell) write
  path from anywhere in the undo/redo module. This is the load-bearing invariant ADR-0016 names
  ("undo NEVER touches built cells") and the one this story explicitly says it only provides the hook
  for (Story 011 constrains it further) — assert the hook exists and nothing in this story's own code
  violates it, even though the full plan-only enforcement is a later story.

**Edge cases to cover**:
- A held Ctrl+Z key-repeat at OS rate → each repeat is exactly one undo step (no acceleration/no
  double-consumption of one repeat event).
- Bounded-stack discard (AC30) and redo-branch clear (AC31) triggered by the SAME new-command commit —
  both effects must be observed from one action, not just tested in isolation.

**Estimated test count**: ~6-7

## Manual QA Checklist

### Windowed play-check over the closed loop (ADVISORY) — first genuinely closed build-and-inhabit cycle
**Why this exists, and why now**: Sprint 6's windowed play-check watched two halves running *side by
side* in one scene (a block got placed, a villager walked somewhere) — there was nothing yet connecting
the two. This sprint's crown is the first time those two halves are actually ONE loop: draw a building,
watch a villager notice it, select it, walk to it, work on it over real time, and watch it become Built
while the job disappears from the queue and the villager wanders off to decide again. This is also the
trigger point Sprint 6's own QA plan named in advance ("the first genuinely broader playtest... becomes
warranted once the fully-closed job loop... lets a villager actually complete a player-placed block
end-to-end... Re-evaluate playtest scope then") — see Playtest Requirements below.

**Verification method**: Manual step-through (windowed, non-`--headless` launch)
**Who must sign off**: qa-lead (or game-designer if a feel/subjective call is disputed)
**Evidence to capture**: a short sequence of screenshots (draw → villager approaches → on-site working
→ Built) plus a short written note in `production/qa/evidence/`

Checklist:
- [ ] Drawing a building, releasing it ("Bau starten"), and watching an idle villager pick it up with no
      manual intervention — no visible delay/hitch at the moment of release, no jarring "teleport to
      job" (the villager should path there cell-by-cell, per Sprint 6's own walk check, now ending at a
      real job site instead of an arbitrary point)
- [ ] The villager visibly works on-site (whatever the on-site "working" tell is — animation, particle,
      or state-color cue) and the cell visibly progresses Planned → UnderConstruction → Built without a
      pop or a frame where the geometry looks wrong (companion check to Sprint 6's block-placement pass,
      now watching a worker-driven completion instead of an instant test-harness write)
- [ ] Two villagers drawn toward the same freshly-released project resolve to each working a distinct
      cell with no visible double-claim confusion or stall (the human-observable companion to the
      headless deterministic-winner assertion — a race-closure regression would likely show here as
      both villagers converging on one cell before it shows in a log)
- [ ] Undo (Ctrl+Z) on a still-Draft/queued cell removes it cleanly with no visual artifact; undo never
      appears to touch an already-Built cell (qualitative companion to building-032's plan-only
      guardrail, not a substitute for the grep-verified test)
- [ ] Toggling pause/warp mid-construction produces the expected effect on build pace without affecting
      camera feel (carried from Sprint 6, now exercised against the real worker-driven build instead of
      the test-harness tick loop)

*ADVISORY — per `/qa-plan` protocol this does not block any story out of Done on its own; the BLOCKING
evidence is the headless crown test (`build_job_cycle_test.gd`) plus the extended
`gameworld_e2e_loop_test.gd`. This is the natural companion check now that the loop is genuinely closed
for the first time.*

### presentation-001 Sub-A evidence capture (ADVISORY at sprint level, BLOCKING for the story itself)
See the dedicated section under Automated Tests Required above — captured separately from the closed-
loop play-check because it is unrelated content (ambient environmental motion) with its own dedicated
evidence file and its own CD-protected sign-off gate.

## Smoke Test Scope

**Baseline**: 682 passing tests (per `sprint-07.md`'s own Sprint 6 actuals: "Test suite 587 → 682, green
on every story commit, zero open regressions").

**What Sprint 7 adds**: up to 12 new/extended test files (6 committed Must + 3 Should + 3 Nice), summing
to roughly **~42-46 tests from the 6 committed Must stories** (building-002 ~5-6, building-004 ~5-6,
building-030 ~6-7, villager-ai-010 ~6-7, villager-ai-011 ~8-9, villager-ai-012 ~9-11 — plus the
`gameworld_e2e_loop_test.gd` extension, which extends existing assertion groups rather than adding a
new count) plus **~10-12 more if both Should tests land** (building-005 ~4-5, building-032 ~6-7 —
presentation-001 contributes at most 1 optional automated flicker assertion, otherwise zero) plus
**~10-12 more if both Nice-Logic/Integration items land** (building-033 ~5-6, building-003 ~5-6) plus
**~2-3 more, non-blocking, if villager-ai-025 lands** (performance suite, Advisory). Target regression
count at sprint close: **~724-730** (committed-only) or **~734-742** (+both Should) or **~744-754**
(+both Nice) — zero failures, zero errors, zero skipped on every BLOCKING file (the Advisory performance
suite may report an over-budget p95 without failing the smoke gate, per Call-out 1).

1. **Full regression suite runs green**: all 682 existing tests PLUS every new/extended Sprint-7 test
   file above via `tests\run-tests.cmd` — 682 is a floor, not a ceiling. **Engine fact carried from
   Sprint 6's actuals**: the GdUnit CLI runner is fail-fast PER SUITE — a single failing assertion halts
   that suite's remaining cases; run each new suite individually at least once during development so a
   later assertion's failure isn't masked by an earlier one silently short-circuiting the file.

2. **THE CROWN + ITS SMOKE-ITEM EXTENSION is smoke item #1 — the sprint's headline gate:**
   - `neues-spiel/tests/integration/villager_ai/build_job_cycle_test.gd` runs headless and green,
     asserting AC12/AC13/AC40/AC40b/AC33 independently — a half-failure must be visible as a distinct
     red, not folded into one pass/fail line, mirroring Sprint 6's scene-004 discipline.
   - **`neues-spiel/tests/integration/scene_world/gameworld_e2e_loop_test.gd` is re-run and green with
     its worker-driven extension in place (Call-out 5)** — grep-verify zero remaining `.claim_job(` or
     `.job_queue =` direct-assignment calls in the file; the villager must reach its job exclusively
     through its own Deciding/F2/claim pass in the assembled scene.
   - The typed-Array crash-class regression call (carried from Sprint 6's AC-E2E-GATE) still fires and
     passes.
   - Both files are re-run at smoke/hand-off time even if they passed at story-completion time — the
     same discipline Sprint 5/6 applied, because this sprint's own critical path (building chain lands
     first, AI chain + crown converge after) means the crown's dependencies land in a specific order
     that makes late-landing wiring breaks the exact risk this smoke item guards against.

3. **Race/ordering assertions for the job loop — named explicitly, not folded into a generic "job
   system works" line (per the delegated QA task and Sprint 6's nav-race precedent, Smoke Scope item
   3):**
   a. **Deterministic winner / clean loser re-decide** (villager-ai-011 AC8 / Edge Case 3): re-run
      `job_claim_attribution_test.gd`'s contention case at smoke time. Because villager-ai-011 does NOT
      depend on building-030 in-sprint, its own test necessarily proves this against a mocked queue —
      **re-confirm the same contention resolution holds inside `build_job_cycle_test.gd`'s real-queue
      environment** (a two-villager race for one real building-030 job resolves to exactly one winner
      by stable order, and the loser cleanly re-decides), not assumed still-true from the mocked-queue
      proof alone.
   b. **Claim released on abandon survives the real queue**: villager-ai-009's AC19 (Sprint 6, dead-
      target exit → report + release claim) was proven against Sprint 6's mocked/duck-typed job queue.
      This sprint, re-verify inside `build_job_cycle_test.gd`'s AC33 case that a revoked/abandoned claim
      genuinely returns the job to the REAL building-030 BUILDING-eligible queue and is re-claimable by
      a second villager — not merely that a release call fired. **This is a QA-defined assertion; no
      story's own Test Evidence section names it** (see Automated Tests Required, villager-ai-012).
   c. **Job completion reporting exactly once**: assert the Built-state write and the job-removed-from-
      queue event each fire exactly once per completed job in `build_job_cycle_test.gd`, including under
      a multi-tick burst (building-029's AC25/AC45 burst rule, Sprint 6) — no double-credit, no
      duplicate completion signal. If building-033 lands, cross-check its AC47 batched-signal-exactly-
      once discipline is consistent with this assertion (both should agree on "one signal per
      frame-of-completions," not conflict).

4. **Building System grep-guard families — extends the Sprint 5/6 precedent to this sprint's new
   lifecycle/queue/undo stories:**
   - Zero physics API calls in the pick/commit path (carried, unaffected by this sprint's stories):
     `rg --glob "*.gd" "intersect_ray|PhysicsDirectSpaceState3D|RayCast3D" src/building_system/` — zero
     matches.
   - Draft cells remain structurally invisible to `claim_job` (building-002/004's own core invariant) —

## Playtest Requirements

| Story | Playtest Goal | Min Sessions | Target Player Type |
|-------|--------------|--------------|-------------------|
| villager-ai-012 (companion, not primary evidence) | Does the fully-closed build-and-inhabit loop ("I built something and someone built it") read as coherent and satisfying to a human watching it end-to-end? | 1 (the windowed play-check above) | qa-lead / game-designer (engineering feel-check) |

**No mandatory external playtest sessions required for this plan.** Every committed Logic/Integration
story's primary evidence path is an automated headless test; the windowed play-check above is an
engineering/feel spot-check (Manual QA Checklist), not a player-feedback session with a questionnaire —
same posture as Sprint 4 and Sprint 6.

**However**: Sprint 6's own QA plan named this sprint in advance as the trigger point for a genuinely
broader playtest — "the first genuinely broader playtest... becomes warranted once the fully-closed job
loop... lets a villager actually complete a player-placed block end-to-end... Re-evaluate playtest scope
then." That condition is now met (villager-ai-012's crown). This plan surfaces the recommendation to
producer/game-designer rather than scheduling it unilaterally: with a real closed loop now in the build,
a small external playtest pool reacting to "draw a house, watch it get built" would be the first
genuinely player-facing signal this project has had. Not a blocker for this sprint's Definition of Done.

- **building-033 and building-003** (Nice) do not carry a playtest-alternate evidence path in their own
  Test Evidence sections (unlike Sprint 5/6's vox-013/014/015 pattern) — both require the automated test
  file if pulled, with no documented-playtest fallback. Flagging so a last-minute Nice pull of either
  does not default to a playtest note the story's own evidence bar does not actually accept.

## Definition of Done — This Sprint

A story is DONE when ALL of the following are true:

- [ ] All acceptance criteria verified — via a passing automated test result. By declared Type:
      **3 Logic** stories (building-002/004, +Should building-032, +Nice building-003 if pulled);
      **6 Integration** stories (building-030, villager-ai-011/012, +Should building-005, +Nice
      building-033 if pulled) — **1 Advisory-Integration** (villager-ai-025, Nice, never a Done
      blocker per Call-out 1) — **1 Visual/Feel** story (presentation-001 Sub-A, ADVISORY at sprint
      level, BLOCKING for its own Done status per Call-out 4)
- [ ] Test file exists at the canonical path listed in this plan's Test Summary table for all in-scope
      stories that land
- [ ] **THE CROWN (villager-ai-012) passes headless**, asserting AC12/AC13/AC40/AC40b/AC33
      independently, using REAL Building System components (no mocks in the crown's own test) — this
      is the sprint's own hard exit condition (Milestone 01 criterion #2 full-depth integration begins
      here) and is not satisfiable by any manual evidence substitute
- [ ] **`gameworld_e2e_loop_test.gd` is extended to the worker-driven path and passes headless**, with
      zero direct `.claim_job(`/`.job_queue =` calls remaining (Call-out 5, smoke item #1's second half)
      — flagged as this plan's own addition since sprint-07.md's DoD prose does not name it explicitly;
      producer/technical-director to confirm this interpretation before it is treated as a hard gate
- [ ] The three named race/ordering assertions (deterministic winner + clean loser re-decide, claim-
      released-on-abandon against the real queue, completion-reported-exactly-once) are present and
      passing, re-checked at smoke time regardless of which individual story's test they live in
- [ ] building-030's AC21/AC36b PROVISIONAL tags are resolved by villager-ai-012's crown test landing
      (Call-out 2) — not left open at sprint close
- [ ] building-032's plan-only undo guardrail (undo/redo never reaches a Built-cell write) is
      grep-verified, zero matches
- [ ] All AStar3D / job-selection APIs (villager-ai-010) confirmed against `docs/engine-reference/godot/`

      `Thread`/`WorkerThreadPool` in Villager AI) remain absent, re-checked against this sprint's new
